experiment_data.hypothesis: Epoch-matched control: training with uniform weighting on filtered data (q>0.5 removed) for exactly 2533 steps (matching content-level 1 epoch of the contaminated data). If PPL is comparable to the full 6103-step D&R run, the D&R benefit comes from data quality not extra training; if PPL is worse, the extra training contributes meaningfully.
experiment_data.notes: Content-level 1 epoch: 153K samples × ~540 avg tokens = ~83M tokens → max_steps=2533. NOT Trainer epoch (9607 steps/315M tokens).

spec.command: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 WANDB_MODE=disabled python training/pretrain_weighted.py --data_path data/scored_data_filtered_q05.jsonl --output_dir /root/autodl-tmp/output/models/detect_remove_q05_epoch_matched_seed42 --model_name models/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --weighting_method uniform --contamination_ratio 0.4 --max_steps 2533 --n_min 2 --tau 0.8 --batch_size 4 --gradient_accumulation_steps 4 --learning_rate 5e-5 --max_length 2048 --seed 42 --save_steps 500 --logging_steps 10 --bf16 --save_total_limit 3

metrics.interpretation: D&R 0.36 PPL advantage over epoch-matched is entirely from multi-epoch training on clean data, not from data quality filtering
